newsitem.title: CHINA: Annan launches first China visit as U.N. chief.
newsitem.headline: Annan launches first China visit as U.N. chief.

text.p: Kofi Annan on Wednesday began his first visit to Beijing as Secretary-General of the United Nations, saying he planned to discuss reform of the global body with one of its most important members.

"I'm looking forward to having a very constructive and useful dialogue with the Chinese authorities and to being able to discuss U.N. reforms and other issues," Annan told reporters after arriving in Beijing.
"I think China plays a very important role in United Nations affairs and has a leadership role in the world," he said.

Annan was scheduled to meet Chinese President Jiang Zemin on Thursday and would also have discussions with Foreign Minister Qian Qichen and economic leaders during what U.N. officials described as a "courtesy visit".
During his five-day visit, Annan would also visit the Pudong economic development zone in Shanghai as well as the ancient northwestern city of Xian, a U.N. official said.
China, a permanent member of the U.N. Security Council, has in the past prided itself on its good relations with United Nations leaders.
Beijing welcomed Annan's appointment last December, even though it had previously supported a second term for his predecessor Boutros Boutros-Ghali.

Chinese state media have repeatedly called for member nations to pay their dues to the United Nations -- a call mainly aimed at Washington, which has helped drive the organisation to the brink of bankruptcy by withholding contributions.
U.N. finance was one of the biggest issues facing the organisation, Annan said, adding that he was confident China would support reforms he planned to implement.
